citation.title: Measurement Validity: A Shared Standard for Qualitative and Quantitative Research
citation.venue_or_publisher: American Political Science Review, Volume 95, Issue 3, pp. 529-546 (Cambridge Core page)
citation.type: journal article; only the Cambridge Core landing page with abstract is in the file

question: Per the abstract: how to assess valid measurement in political science with one framework for quantitative and qualitative scholars; separating measurement issues from disputes about concepts; context-specific measurement; and the main types of validation.

limitations.point: The file holds only a Cambridge Core landing page with the abstract, not the full text. The reference list and article body are not in the text; the References section is empty, and the access section says the article is purchase-only and temporarily unavailable. Nothing beyond the abstract was read, so no definitions, proxies or findings are recorded.

pages_read: Abstract only (one paragraph, section 'Abstract'), plus page furniture (article contents, access options, empty references, comments). The extracted text has no authors field; author names come from the page's author links (Robert Adcock, David Collier) and the year from the published date 2001/09. Full text not present.

abstract_statement.claim: The abstract says the authors offer an account of the three main types of validation most relevant to political scientists, and a shared framework for measurement validity.
abstract_statement.quote: we seek to establish a shared framework that allows quantitative and qualitative scholars to assess more effectively, and communicate about, issues of valid measurement.
